supporting_observations.claim: The approved CobaltVault agent ran on FILE-HD-01 as HARBOR-DENTAL\svc-bkp, using the inventoried executable and the expected CobaltVault destination.

The observed CobaltVault proxy activity was brief and small: the connection logged 1,449 client-to-server bytes and 24,228 server-to-client bytes; a later attempt received proxy status 407. These records do not show the hundreds-of-megabytes transfer described in the alert.
The CobaltVault process exited shortly after those proxy attempts, at 13:45:58 UTC.

At 14:04 UTC, FILE-HD-01 made a short proxy connection to downloads.cloud.com with a curl user agent. Cloud.com is not among the listed approved services, but the record shows only small byte counts and does not establish an upload or its contents.

At 14:05 UTC, FILE-HD-01 initiated a connection to WS-OHADDAD-01 on RPC endpoint-mapper port 135. This is in the direction opposite the stated practice that remote administration is performed from WS-OHADDAD-01; the connection alone does not establish that remote administration occurred.

WS-OHADDAD-01 requested Kerberos service tickets for FILE-HD-01 shortly before and after the alert time, which is consistent with access from the designated IT workstation but does not prove that the approved patching procedure ran.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include an egress flow or byte-count record identifying the reported hundreds-of-megabytes transfer or its destination. The nearby CobaltVault proxy records show only small transfers (T010-00322, T010-00325).
Proxy records identify the client host and user agent for the cloud.com connection, but do not attribute it to a process or show the transferred content (T010-00515, T010-00516).
The RPC connection to WS-OHADDAD-01 is recorded, but the supplied records do not show the RPC operation, its initiating process, or a resulting command execution (T010-00528, T010-00529, T010-00530).
claims_not_established: Whether the alert’s large transfer actually occurred, and if so, its destination, initiating process, content, and authorization.
Whether the CobaltVault backup completed elsewhere or was blocked; the observed attempts alone do not establish either outcome (T010-00322, T010-00329, T010-00336).
Whether the downloads.cloud.com connection involved an upload, data staging, or benign activity (T010-00515, T010-00516).
Whether the FILE-HD-01-to-WS-OHADDAD-01 RPC connection executed remote administration or was otherwise authorized (T010-00528, T010-00529, T010-00530).
Whether the scheduled svc-claimsync password rotation and manual job update occurred as planned; the supplied records do not directly document those actions.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve firewall, NetFlow, proxy, or packet-level records for FILE-HD-01 covering the alert interval, including destination, direction, byte counts, and any direct-egress traffic.
Obtain FILE-HD-01 process/network telemetry and CobaltVault agent logs to determine whether a large transfer occurred and which process initiated it.
Inspect proxy and endpoint records for the downloads.cloud.com connection, including process attribution, request method, byte counts, and destination details.
Collect RPC/WMI and endpoint process-creation telemetry for the 14:05 connection between FILE-HD-01 and WS-OHADDAD-01, and verify against IT change or patching records.
Verify the svc-claimsync rotation and job-update records for the scheduled 13:30 UTC change.
